title: Aporia - Early Access
author: W2DGAMES
selftext:
I’ve just released an early tech demo of Act I of Aporia. You wake on a beach with no memory, mend a holed boat, row out to rescue strangers who woke on the islets around you, and turn a bare island into a village together.

Play free in your browser: [https://wavedash.com/games/aporia](https://wavedash.com/games/aporia)

**How it’s made**

Nearly all of the code was written by Claude Code, with me as designer and director. Some details that might interest people here:

**Stack:** Rust and Bevy, compiled to WebAssembly and rendered with WebGPU, so it runs in a desktop browser.

Design decisions are logged: every decision is recorded in a decisions file so new sessions don’t relitigate settled choices.

Simulation separate from rendering: the game rules live in a pure Rust simulation crate with its own tests. The game layer only reads that state and sends commands to it.

Content is data: items, recipes, characters and story pages live in data files. A generated “content map” shows every item and how the player progresses, including any gaps.

Autotests that play the game: they open a window, play through each feature, and save screenshots that Claude and I review after visual changes.

Art: models come from Blender Python scripts. Trees, bushes, grass and terrain textures are generated in code. 

**What to expect**

It’s very early: Act I only, with rough edges and bugs, and saves will break or be wiped between updates. It will improve a lot.

I’d really value feedback on the game, a lot of what's already designed is actually locked for future acts as the scope is much bigger than what's available on ACT I :)
